steps.title: challenge it (attempt 1)
steps.expected: RIG-17: matched on the prompt's own text (EncounterDirector, not the bramblebun, owns it) rather than entity relatedness, so this presses a real engage offer and refuses a fainted-ally message like "Ripplet is out of the fight"/"Put Moss away" instead of misfiring into it.

steps.title: let the fight stage
steps.expected: the combat camera acquires both combatants

steps.title: trim it with quick attacks (do not kill it)
steps.expected: the target is WEAKENED as close to zero HP as this fight will safely bear -- not defeated, a defeated wild cannot be caught -- computed from the fight's own real per-hit damage rather than a guessed hit count or a guessed HP-fraction floor.
steps.observation: RIG, 2026-08-31: combat_quick x20 KILLED a 106 HP target, so a fixed times: 3 (S02's own proven opener) replaced it -- correctly avoiding a kill, but measured directly (gate-f-run-20260902T053310Z-s03enginefix) landing anywhere from 57% to 75% of max HP depending on the creature's own defence, the FLAT part of hp_factor's curve. A fixed enemy_hp_fraction 0.3 floor (this step's own immediately-prior version) fixed that but was still a guessed number, not a computed one -- called out directly by the owner in this session, 2026-09-02 ('if 5 presses took 70 health you could do another 2 without killing it. why wouldnt you? ... you can surely calculate what needs to be done'). chip_to_floor (operator_harness.gd, added for this) reads the live enemy hp before and after every swing and learns the actual per-hit damage this fight is dealing -- combat_math.gd::rolled_damage()'s only per-swing randomness against a fixed target is its +/-10% variance roll, so one real hit already bounds every later one -- and refuses the next swing only once the largest hit seen so far, scaled by safety_factor (1.25, past the 1.1/0.9=1.222 worst-case roll swing), would not survive. No fixed floor anywhere in this step; it chips exactly as far as the specific creature in front of it allows.

steps.title: aim and throw until caught, or out of tries (attempt 1)
steps.expected: the target is caught, or every allotted throw against it is spent -- a missed throw does not end the fight (catching.json's own cooldown exists so a failed catch can be re-thrown once the wobble clears; combat_manager.gd re-engages the same target on a miss), so this keeps throwing at the SAME chipped-down target instead of treating one orb as the whole attempt.
steps.observation: Owner directive, this session: "we should chip down then throw orbs til we catch." The ladder used to spend exactly one orb per numbered attempt (arm aim, track, throw once, wait) and then move on regardless of outcome -- discarding real, intended-to-be-retried catch chances the moment a single throw missed, even though nothing about the game ends the fight on a miss. throw_until_caught (operator_harness.gd, added for this) re-arms the aim, re-tracks the live target and throws again, up to max_throws times, stopping the instant the party actually grows.

steps.title: wait for the world to own input before this walk
steps.expected: no narrative modal or combat is holding locomotion when this walk starts
steps.observation: T2-GATEF-RUN6 modal-holds-locomotion audit, upgraded per FINDING-CAPSTONE3-S03-CATCH-LOOP-STALL-2026-09-01. This step used to be a one-shot `assert`, diagnostic only: it recorded that the previous fight/catch had not finished unwinding but did not wait for it, so attempts b-j walked straight into 'the interaction arbiter is DISABLED... input_context combat' every time. `wait_until` polls the same check instead of sampling it once, so the next attempt's walk starts only once combat has actually closed and the world owns input again -- CD-3's rule applied to the retry ladder's own seam, not just to a single wait.

steps.title: focus the Revive draught
steps.expected: T2-GATEF-RUN5/GAME-9/RIG-24 (S03-56d/S03-56f) already proved fixed-offset focus_move fragile in this same bag once acquisitions or spends shift the grid: a positional "3 cells right of slot 0" assumed a fresh save's fill order, and this ladder's own telemetry (gate-f-run-20260901T220548Z-s03fix attempts 3-4) shows it silently landing on the wrong item once earlier presses in this same recovery block had already shifted the grid, so every recovery reported PASS while reviving nothing and party size stayed capped at 2 (FINDING-S03-CATCH-LOOP-REVIVE-SLOT-2026-09-02). focus_item reads the cursor and sends real ui_left/ui_right the way a player reads the bag, regardless of where Revive actually sits.

steps.title: close the shell for real
steps.expected: Whichever branch was taken, the shell is in ordinary grid focus by now, so this closes it -- the same unconditional 4-press sequence S03-39e..j already validated in both the fainted and nobody-fainted case.

steps.title: cycle to a live party member before attempt 2 (T2-BUILDPLACE)
steps.expected: REORDERED after a 3-attempt verification chain (ralph/reports/gate-f-run-20260901T220548Z-s03fix). Revive-then-cycle, not cycle-then-revive: when BOTH party members are fainted at once (attempt-b's own fight fainted the second member here), cycle_active() run FIRST has no live member to switch to and is a no-op, and a revive run afterward heals a creature without ever making it the ACTIVE one -- encounter_director.gd's `_ally` pointer stays on whichever (still-fainted) creature was active when the block started, so interaction_offer()'s priority-100 lockout persists even though someone in the roster is healthy again. Reviving FIRST, then cycling, means cycle_active() has a genuinely live member to find by the time it runs. autoload/party.gd::cycle_active() remains a documented no-op when the active creature is already the only healthy one, so this is still safe to run unconditionally.

Revive-then-cycle, not cycle-then-revive: when BOTH party members are fainted at once (attempt-b's own fight fainted the second member here), cycle_active() run FIRST has no live member to switch to and is a no-op, and a revive run afterward heals a creature without ever making it the ACTIVE one -- encounter_director.gd's `_ally` pointer stays on whichever (still-fainted) creature was active when the block started, so interaction_offer()'s priority-100 lockout persists even though someone in the roster is healthy again. Reviving FIRST, then cycling, means cycle_active() has a genuinely live member to find by the time it runs. autoload/party.gd::cycle_active() remains a documented no-op when the active creature is already the only healthy one, so this is still safe to run unconditionally.

steps.title: let the party swap finish
steps.expected: encounter_director.gd::summon_active_creature() is async; the newly-active creature's body needs a few frames to stand up before the next engage is attempted.

steps.title: wait for the world to own input before attempt 7
steps.expected: Both branches above converge on a closed shell and a settled party swap; the world must have input back before the next attempt's walk starts.

steps.title: walk to a live bramblebun (attempt 7)
steps.expected: RIG-16: tracks a live bramblebun's own position every frame instead of a fixed cluster-centre coordinate.
steps.observation: RIG-F5/GAME-F3. `within: 4.5` is what handed the interact button to a harvest node: prompt_arbiter.gd is 'highest priority first, then NEAREST', engage and gather are both priority 0, and from 4.5 m out a node at half a metre wins every time. Four of the twenty authored village nodes sit inside the practice cluster's own 15 m disc, deliberately -- harvest.json's own _why_gate_b_three_beds put them on 'the practice-path loop the first day already walks' -- so the collision is structural and the fix is to stand at the creature, which is what a player does. 2.0 rather than 1.8: RIG-F5 measured a bramblebun 0.22 m up a slope failing a 1.8 m close_3d check at 1.81 m in 3D, and named 2.0 as the floor.

steps.title: challenge it (attempt 7)
steps.expected: RIG-17: matched on the prompt's own text (EncounterDirector, not the bramblebun, owns it) rather than entity relatedness, so this presses a real engage offer and refuses a fainted-ally message like "Ripplet is out of the fight"/"Put Moss away" instead of misfiring into it.

steps.title: let the fight stage
steps.expected: the combat camera acquires both combatants

steps.title: trim it with quick attacks (do not kill it)
steps.expected: the target is WEAKENED as close to zero HP as this fight will safely bear -- not defeated, a defeated wild cannot be caught -- computed from the fight's own real per-hit damage rather than a guessed hit count or a guessed HP-fraction floor.
steps.observation: RIG, 2026-08-31: combat_quick x20 KILLED a 106 HP target, so a fixed times: 3 (S02's own proven opener) replaced it -- correctly avoiding a kill, but measured directly (gate-f-run-20260902T053310Z-s03enginefix) landing anywhere from 57% to 75% of max HP depending on the creature's own defence, the FLAT part of hp_factor's curve. A fixed enemy_hp_fraction 0.3 floor (this step's own immediately-prior version) fixed that but was still a guessed number, not a computed one -- called out directly by the owner in this session, 2026-09-02 ('if 5 presses took 70 health you could do another 2 without killing it. why wouldnt you? ... you can surely calculate what needs to be done'). chip_to_floor (operator_harness.gd, added for this) reads the live enemy hp before and after every swing and learns the actual per-hit damage this fight is dealing -- combat_math.gd::rolled_damage()'s only per-swing randomness against a fixed target is its +/-10% variance roll, so one real hit already bounds every later one -- and refuses the next swing only once the largest hit seen so far, scaled by safety_factor (1.25, past the 1.1/0.9=1.222 worst-case roll swing), would not survive. No fixed floor anywhere in this step; it chips exactly as far as the specific creature in front of it allows.

steps.title: aim and throw until caught, or out of tries (attempt 7)
steps.expected: the target is caught, or every allotted throw against it is spent -- a missed throw does not end the fight (catching.json's own cooldown exists so a failed catch can be re-thrown once the wobble clears; combat_manager.gd re-engages the same target on a miss), so this keeps throwing at the SAME chipped-down target instead of treating one orb as the whole attempt.
steps.observation: Owner directive, this session: "we should chip down then throw orbs til we catch." The ladder used to spend exactly one orb per numbered attempt (arm aim, track, throw once, wait) and then move on regardless of outcome -- discarding real, intended-to-be-retried catch chances the moment a single throw missed, even though nothing about the game ends the fight on a miss. throw_until_caught (operator_harness.gd, added for this) re-arms the aim, re-tracks the live target and throws again, up to max_throws times, stopping the instant the party actually grows.

steps.title: wait for the world to own input before this walk
steps.expected: no narrative modal or combat is holding locomotion when this walk starts
steps.observation: T2-GATEF-RUN6 modal-holds-locomotion audit, upgraded per FINDING-CAPSTONE3-S03-CATCH-LOOP-STALL-2026-09-01. steps.title: focus the Revive draught

steps.expected: T2-BUILDPLACE ROUND 2 (FINDING-T2-BUILDPLACE-2026-08-30.md, round 3): replaces the round-2 fix's blind creature_recall dismiss here. That dismiss cleared the blanket "is out of the fight" override (still true and still needed -- see the note below) but ALSO zeroed _ally, and encounter_director.gd::can_challenge() refuses a null ally exactly like a fainted one (line ~1568). Live-confirmed this round: with the dismiss in place, Bryn's own _on_challenged() (trainer_npc.gd) read can_challenge()==false and opened his 'defeated' conversation instead of 'challenge' for every subsequent replay -- no fight ever started, so S03-48/S03-50's combat_quick presses hit nothing, S03-51a's level-up capture had no level-up to catch, and the training rung's own evidence (Section L.4 T05/T06, GF-14-COMBAT-02) was never real. autoload/party.gd::cycle_active() skips fainted/resting members and is a documented no-op when the active creature is already the only healthy one (returns false, revision untouched), so pressing it here is safe regardless of outcome: if the catch loop's deployed ally fainted, this moves `active` to a live party member and encounter_director.gd::_sync_active_creature() (polled every frame off party.revision in _process()) dismisses the fainted body and summons the new active one; if the ally did not faint, this just cycles to a different live member, which costs nothing. Either way _ally ends up live (non-null, non-fainted) before Bryn's challenge, clearing interaction_offer()'s blanket override the same way the old dismiss did, without breaking can_challenge().

steps.observation: Tightened again 2026-09-02 (second pass): the previous within:1.2, computed from ONE run's measured 4.0m camp-to-bed separation (< half of it, so the walk could never land closer to camp than to the bed by the triangle inequality), was not tight enough on a later run whose relative stick-placement (S03-121n/131n/141n) happened to land the pieces closer together: that run's own S03-205a reported 'walked 2.7 m ... in 35 walking frames' -- a short, nearly-direct walk, consistent with a SMALLER separation than 4.0m that time -- and S03-205b still read camp's own 'Rest until morning' instead of the bed's 'Rest a Creature'. The relative placement offsets (a fixed stick deflection for a fixed frame count, S03-121n/131n/141n) do not guarantee a fixed separation between pieces run to run, so a within tuned to one run's measured gap is not safe in general -- only a tighter margin buys more headroom against that variance. 0.6 halves the previous figure; if a future run's own placed_buildings measurement shows a separation under roughly 1.2 m (where 0.6 stops guaranteeing the triangle-inequality property), this needs ralph/OWNER-0902-REST-VISIBILITY's own fix (its name is literally this problem), not a third harness-side tightening -- a shared interact-prompt RADIUS two pieces of furniture can be placed inside of is not something a walk-stopping-distance can out-tune forever.
